# Overview

This report demonstrates a reproducible workflow for analysing simulated longitudinal PET/MRI and cognitive data.

The aim is to show a protected public example of:

- simulated PET/MRI-style data organization;
- neuroimaging-style quality-control logic;
- paired longitudinal completeness checks;
- descriptive summaries and visualization;
- mixed-effects longitudinal modeling;
- within-person and between-person PET marker decomposition;
- change-score sensitivity analysis.

This report uses simulated data only. It does not contain real participant data, clinical data, raw neuroimaging files, unpublished project materials, or collaborator-owned results.

# Data protection and scope

All data in this repository are simulated. The variable names are generic and are used only to demonstrate workflow structure, quality-control logic, and statistical modeling principles.

The workflow is inspired by common analytical tasks in cognitive neuroscience and PET/MRI research, including the analysis of molecular imaging markers, structural MRI-derived measures, and cognitive performance across repeated assessments.

# Workflow structure

The repository is organized as follows:

```{r}
list.files("R")
```

The scripts are intended to be run in this order:

```text
R/01_simulate_data.R
R/02_qc_checks.R
R/03_descriptives.R
R/04_longitudinal_models.R
R/05_change_score_models.R
```

# Simulated dataset

The simulated dataset contains repeated observations for each participant. The core variables include:

```text
participant_id
timepoint
age_baseline
sex
scanner_site
pet_marker_bpnd
mri_volume_index
memory_score
registration_qc
motion_qc
processing_qc
```

The PET marker is represented as a generic binding-potential-style variable. The MRI variable is represented as a generic volume index. The cognitive variable is represented as a generic memory score.

# Quality control

Neuroimaging workflows require explicit quality-control decisions before statistical modeling. In this template, QC checks include:

- missingness checks;
- implausible value checks;
- registration QC flags;
- motion QC flags;
- processing QC flags;
- paired longitudinal completeness checks.

# Longitudinal mixed-effects models

The longitudinal analysis demonstrates repeated-measures modelling using participant-level random intercepts.

Three models are included:

```text
Model 1: Basic longitudinal model
Model 2: Within-person / between-person PET model
Model 3: PET by age interaction model
```

The basic model estimates memory score as a function of time, PET marker, MRI volume index, baseline age, sex, scanner site, and participant-level random intercept.

The within-person / between-person model separates PET marker variation within individuals over time from between-person differences in average PET marker level.

The PET by age interaction model demonstrates how one might test whether the association between PET marker and memory differs by baseline age.

# Change-score sensitivity analysis

The change-score analysis uses paired T1/T2 data to calculate:

```text
delta_memory = memory_T2 - memory_T1
delta_pet_marker = PET_T2 - PET_T1
delta_mri_volume = MRI_T2 - MRI_T1
```

It also includes percentage-change versions as a simple sensitivity analysis.

Three models are included:

```text
Model 1: Raw change-score model
Model 2: Change-score PET by age interaction model
Model 3: Percent-change sensitivity model
```

# Interpretation

This workflow demonstrates how a protected public repository can show relevant PET/MRI analysis skills without exposing real data or unpublished results.

The main strengths demonstrated are:

- clear project organisation;
- reproducible R scripts;
- explicit QC decision rules;
- paired longitudinal completeness checks;
- mixed-effects modelling for repeated observations;
- within-person and between-person decomposition;
- change-score sensitivity analysis;
- report-ready tables and figures.

Because the data are simulated, the numerical results should not be interpreted as scientific findings. The purpose of this repository is methodological demonstration.

# Limitations

This template is intentionally simplified. It does not include raw NIfTI images, BIDS validation, PET preprocessing, MRI segmentation, partial-volume correction, image registration, or scanner harmonization.

Those steps would normally be part of a full neuroimaging project. Here, the focus is on the downstream data-analytic workflow: QC tracking, longitudinal modeling, sensitivity analysis, and transparent reporting.

# Reproducibility note

This report was generated using Quarto and R. The repository is designed so that all tables and figures can be regenerated from the scripts using simulated data.
